source.ref: Maharashtra Stamp Act, 1958, Sch. I Art. 63 (added by Mah. 12 of 2006 w.e.f. 1-5-2006; rates subst. by Mah. 20 of 2015 s.20(34) w.e.f. 24-4-2015)
source.quoted_text: Sch I Art. 63 (both columns): 'Works Contract, that is to say, a contract for works and labour or services involving transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) in its execution and includes a sub-contract — (a) where the amount or value set forth in such contract does not exceed rupees ten lakh — Five hundred rupees; (b) where it exceeds rupees ten lakh — Five hundred rupees plus 0.1 per cent of the amount above rupees ten lakh subject to maximum of rupees twenty-five lakhs.' [Rates subst. by Mah. 20 of 2015; prior: Rs 100 + Rs 100 per Rs 1,00,000 above Rs 10 lakh, max Rs 5 lakh.]

pending_verification.reason: STALE — Mah. 9 of 2025 s.2(16), in force 14-10-2024, substituted the Art 63 threshold ("ten lakh" -> "five lakh") and the rate ("0.1 per cent." -> "0.3 per cent."). This version still encodes the pre-amendment 10L/0.1% and is roughly 3x under for current contracts: a Rs 5cr works contract is Rs 1,49,000, not the Rs 49,500 this returns. Refuses from the amendment date; the back-catalogue below that date remains correct and still computes. Founder to verify and encode the new era from the India Code consolidated Act.

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: HIGH (official IGR, both columns). Marginal-with-cap: ≤ Rs 10 lakh → Rs 500; above → Rs 500 + 0.1% of the excess over Rs 10 lakh, TOTAL capped at Rs 25,00,000. Input: contract_value. The cap is read as applying to the whole duty (Rs 500 + the 0.1% component) — confirm. THE WORKS-vs-SERVICE FORK IS HUGE IN MAHARASHTRA: a Rs 5 crore contract is Rs 49,500 as a works contract but Rs 100 as an Art 5(h)(B) service agreement (≈495×) — unlike Delhi (Rs 50 vs Rs 50) and Karnataka (Rs 200 vs Rs 200), where the classification is duty-neutral. Route via the MH-works-vs-service tree; the pre-2015 version (Rs 100 + Rs 100/lakh, max Rs 5 lakh) is a back-catalogue item.

source.ref: Maharashtra Stamp Act, 1958, Sch. I Art. 5(h)(B)
source.quoted_text: Sch I Art. 5 (AGREEMENT OR ITS RECORDS OR MEMORANDUM OF AN AGREEMENT), clause (h)(B) (both columns): '(B) if not otherwise provided for — One hundred rupees.' Cross-heading in Sch I: 'HIRING AGREEMENT or agreement for service, see Agreement (Article 5).'

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH. Art 5 expressly routes 'agreement for service' here; (h)(B) residual = Rs 100. CAUTION: Art 5 has many specific sub-clauses that override the residual (e.g. (g-a) development agreements = conveyance rate; (h)(A) works-like contracts at 0.1%/0.2% of the contract amount) — the questionnaire must rule those out before landing on (h)(B). Given the 495× works-vs-service gap in MH, mis-routing here is the highest-consequence classification error in the corpus; effective_from set at the 2015 coverage floor (exact amendment date to confirm).

source.ref: Maharashtra Stamp Act, 1958, Sch. I Art. 63 as it stood before Mah. Act 20 of 2015 s.20(34)
source.quoted_text: Sch I Art. 63 PRIOR to Mah. 20 of 2015 (IGR footnotes 7 & 8, verbatim): '(a) ... does not exceed rupees ten lakh — One hundred rupees'; '(b) where it exceeds rupees ten lakh — One hundred rupees plus one hundred rupees for every rupees 1,00,000 or part thereof, above rupees ten lakh, subject to the maximum of rupees five lakh.' Substituted w.e.f. 24-4-2015 by the current Rs 500 + 0.1% / Rs 25 lakh structure.

notes_for_reviewer: BACK-CATALOGUE (2015-01-01 → 2015-04-23): Rs 100 + Rs 100 for every Rs 1,00,000 OR PART THEREOF above Rs 10 lakh, total capped at Rs 5,00,000. 'Or part thereof' is a CEILING step, modelled exactly with ceil_div — a plain division would under-charge every partial slab (e.g. Rs 10,50,000 → 1 full slab = Rs 200, not Rs 150).
